# Restore narration: from `plan_check` FAIL to the closing line Before the first `plan_check`, the restore had already called `start brainstorm`, then `skip brainstorm` with reason `resume: /work/app/.worktrees/retire-legacy/doc/specs/2026-03-09-retire-legacy-parsers.md`, then `start plan`. Tool results 1–2 recorded the plan as **tracked and clean**: `ls-files` exited 0 and `status --porcelain` printed nothing. Plan repair can therefore restore it with `git checkout` if needed, and no temp copy is made. --- **Tool result 3: `plan_check` → FAIL (400 findings)** Per the call table's "implement with task plan" row, a FAIL means I enter `## Plan repair`. The input is the brief's task snapshot, which I read for evidence and never rewrite. - **Baseline routing.** There are no `baseline-line` or substantive `open-questions` findings, so the baseline continuation does not apply. I go straight to citation repair. - **Classification.** All 400 findings match one row: - Check: `paths-exist`. - Reason: `Modify: path "

" does not exist`. - Evidence part 1: each row's owning task is complete in the snapshot. Task `[2] W1: Delete legacy/parsers tree` owns 200 rows and task `[3] W1: Delete legacy/fixtures tree` owns 197 rows; both are `✓`. **Tool call** (once per finding path `

`, 400 calls): `git -C /work/app/.worktrees/retire-legacy log --diff-filter=D --format=%h -1 --

` **Tool result 4:** each call prints a hash. The deletion evidence is present for all 400 paths, so every finding is classified and nothing stops the repair. **Round 1 edit.** I drop the 400 `Modify:` rows from the Files blocks of Tasks 2 and 3 in `/work/app/.worktrees/retire-legacy/doc/plans/2026-03-09-retire-legacy-parsers.md`. Nothing else changes: - task names, count, order and waves stay the same; - `Solo:` lines and the owner column stay the same; - no other task text is touched. **Tool call:** `plan_check({ planPath: "/work/app/.worktrees/retire-legacy/doc/plans/2026-03-09-retire-legacy-parsers.md" })` **Tool result 5:** PASS, after 1 of at most 3 rounds. The plan was tracked and clean before the loop, so I commit the plan alone. **Tool call:** ```bash git -C /work/app/.worktrees/retire-legacy add -- doc/plans/2026-03-09-retire-legacy-parsers.md && git -C /work/app/.worktrees/retire-legacy commit -q -m "resume: plan citation repair - 400 findings" -- doc/plans/2026-03-09-retire-legacy-parsers.md ``` → exit 0. --- **Return to the call table from `skip plan R`** 1. **Tool call:** `phase_tracker skip plan`, reason `resume: pasted brief`. The brief text was supplied inline rather than as a named file, so `R` uses `"pasted brief"`. → ok. 2. **Tool call:** `phase_tracker start implement`. The fresh `plan_check` stamp from result 5 admits it. → ok. - The brief shows `→ implement` with no substep, so there is no `substep` call. 3. **Feasibility check before `init`:** - Pending-suffix order holds: the only `○` task, [5], trails every non-pending task. - Not all tasks are complete or skipped, so implement will not auto-complete. 4. **Tool call:** `plan_tracker init`, using the snapshot verbatim (names, order, statuses) → ok: - `{ name: "W1: Inventory legacy parsers", status: "complete" }` - `{ name: "W1: Delete legacy/parsers tree", status: "complete" }` - `{ name: "W1: Delete legacy/fixtures tree", status: "complete" }` - `{ name: "W2: Point imports at the new parser", status: "in_progress" }` - `{ name: "W3: Update the parser guide", status: "pending" }` --- **Printed lines, in order:** ``` Repaired plan: 400 findings (paths-exist) Gate history not restored; re-validating `W2: Point imports at the new parser` before any stage advance ``` Next comes the check 6 line, either `Standing grant active: ` or `No standing grant.`. I can't print it here because the input doesn't give check 6's grant result. Work then continues in subagent-driven-development. It first re-validates `W2: Point imports at the new parser` by re-running its `Tests:`, then resumes the task loop from task [4].
